name: Cook Islands
prevalence_note: The Cook Islands Financial Intelligence Unit publishes a live scams page and a specific warning that people posing as Bank of South Pacific staff have been contacting BSP customers over WhatsApp and Google Meet. Together with BSP Cook Islands, CIFIU has also described advance-fee fraud sold through Facebook ads that promise a large return within a day after a small deposit into a local 'agent' account.
cross_border_note: CIFIU notes that some of the bogus BSP callers appear to use Gmail accounts and that some calls seem to come from Pakistan or India, and that a BSP logo on a profile is not proof of a real banker. The islands are reached on +682; digits that merely resemble a Rarotonga line, or a familiar logo on a calling app, are not enough.

scams.name: Fake BSP staff on WhatsApp or Google Meet
scams.name_en: CIFIU warning: callers on WhatsApp or Google Meet impersonating Bank of South Pacific and seeking PINs, passwords, one-time codes or card data
context_keywords: profile photo with a bank logo

red_flag_keywords.text: give your BSP PIN on WhatsApp
full card number and security code
join this Google Meet with the bank

scams.signals_en: CIFIU warns scammers contact BSP customers on WhatsApp and Google Meet (sometimes using a bank logo) to demand passwords, PINs, OTPs or card details, and may record voices to imitate them. BSP never uses calling apps to reach customers.
scams.legit_en: Bank of South Pacific Cook Islands never contacts customers on WhatsApp or calling apps. Real fraud or payment queries go through published bank channels and never ask for passwords, PINs, OTPs or full card details in chat.
bait_tactics: End the WhatsApp or Google Meet session and say any bank query will be raised only through the official BSP Cook Islands channel, not through a calling app.
Refuse to speak a PIN, a one-time passcode or a card number, and say the voice will not be recorded for a 'verification'.
Tell the caller the incident will be reported to CIFIU and to Police in Rarotonga, and that the chat will not continue.

scams.name: Facebook advance-fee 'agent' deposit for a same-day windfall
scams.name_en: CIFIU and BSP Cook Islands warning: advance-fee fraud via Facebook ads that ask for a small deposit into a local agent account in return for a much larger same-day payout
context_keywords: local agent account in the Cook Islands
loan or grant released after a fee

red_flag_keywords.text: pay a fee before the prize is released
deposit into the agent's personal account
send crypto or a gift card instead

scams.signals_en: BSP Cook Islands and CIFIU warn of advance-fee scams for loans, grants, gifts or investments, such as Facebook ads promising huge same-day payouts after a small NZD/CKD deposit to a local 'agent' account, using fake videos or celebrity names.
scams.legit_en: A real Cook Islands bank or licensed lender never demands an upfront fee into a private 'agent' account, crypto or gift cards before releasing a loan, prize or return. CIFIU advises pausing, verifying and reporting to Police.
bait_tactics: Say the supposed return will be checked with CIFIU or the bank before any deposit is made into an agent account.
Ask why a lawful payment would have to travel by crypto, a gift card or a personal 'agent' account rather than a published bank channel.
Offer to telephone the friend who appears in the testimonial on a known number, to see whether that person really made the video.
